q-105547.name: Question 1
q-105547.problem: The acceleration of a cyclist is $1.5\,{\text{m/s}}^{2}.$ What is the cyclist's acceleration in ${\text{km/s}}^{2}?$
q-105547.worked_solution:
We are given the units $\frac{\text{m}}{{\text{s}}^{2}},$ and we want to convert this into $\frac{\text{km}}{{\text{s}}^{2}}.$ To figure out what we need to multiply by, we can set up an equation to help us:

$$
\frac{\text{m}}{{\text{s}}^{2}}\cdot \,\frac{?}{?}=\frac{\text{km}}{{\text{s}}^{2}}
$$

We want to replace $\text{m}$ with $\text{km}.$ To get rid of $\text{m},$ we can put $\text{m}$ in the denominator so that it cancels out. To introduce $\text{km},$ we can put $\text{km}$ in the numerator.

$$
\frac{\cancel{\text{m}}}{{\text{s}}^{2}}\cdot \frac{\text{km}}{\cancel{\text{m}}}=\frac{\text{km}}{{\text{s}}^{2}}
$$

So, our conversion formula is

$$
\frac{\text{m}}{{\text{s}}^{2}}\cdot \frac{\text{km}}{\text{m}}=\frac{\text{km}}{{\text{s}}^{2}}.
$$

Now that we have our conversion formula, we need to determine the correct numbers to use, and apply it.

- The acceleration given in the problem statement is $1.5\,\frac{\text{m}}{{\text{s}}^{2}}.$

- There are $1\,000$ meters per kilometer. Taking the reciprocal, there are $\frac{1}{1\,000}$ kilometers per meter.

Applying our conversion formula, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}1.5\,\frac{\text{m}}{{\text{s}}^{2}} & =1.5\,\frac{\text{m}}{{\text{s}}^{2}}\cdot \frac{1}{1\,000}\,\frac{\text{km}}{\text{m}} \\  & =1.5\cdot \frac{1}{1\,000}(\frac{\cancel{\text{m}}}{{\text{s}}^{2}}\cdot \frac{\text{km}}{\cancel{\text{m}}}) \\  & =0.001\,5\,\frac{\text{km}}{{\text{s}}^{2}}.\end{aligned}
$$

Thus, the acceleration of the cyclist is $0.001\,5\,\text{km}/{\text{s}}^{2}.$

q-105547.html:
Question 1
?

The acceleration of a cyclist is 1.5m/s2. What is the cyclist's acceleration in km/s2?

a
0.15km/s2
b
150km/s2
c
0.0015km/s2
d
0.015km/s2
e
15km/s2
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

We are given the units ms2, and we want to convert this into kms2. To figure out what we need to multiply by, we can set up an equation to help us: ms2⋅??=kms2

We want to replace m with km. To get rid of m, we can put m in the denominator so that it cancels out. To introduce km, we can put km in the numerator. ms2⋅kmm=kms2

So, our conversion formula is ms2⋅kmm=kms2.

Now that we have our conversion formula, we need to determine the correct numbers to use, and apply it.

  • The acceleration given in the problem statement is 1.5ms2.
  • There are 1000 meters per kilometer. Taking the reciprocal, there are 11000 kilometers per meter.

Applying our conversion formula, we have 1.5ms2=1.5ms2⋅11000kmm=1.5⋅11000(ms2⋅kmm)=0.0015kms2.

Thus, the acceleration of the cyclist is 0.0015km/s2.

q-105551.name: Question 2
q-105551.problem: A cruise ship on the high seas travels at a speed of $972$ centimeters per second. What is the speed of the ship in meters per second?
q-105551.worked_solution:
We are given the units $\frac{\text{cm}}{\text{s}},$ and we want to convert this into $\frac{\text{m}}{\text{s}}.$ To figure out what we need to multiply by, we can set up an equation to help us:

$$
\frac{\text{cm}}{\text{s}}\cdot \,\frac{?}{?}=\frac{\text{m}}{\text{s}}
$$

We want to replace $\text{cm}$ with $\text{m}.$ To get rid of $\text{cm},$ we can put $\text{cm}$ in the denominator so that it cancels out. To introduce $\text{m},$ we can put $\text{m}$ in the numerator.

$$
\frac{\cancel{\text{cm}}}{\text{s}}\cdot \frac{\text{m}}{\cancel{\text{cm}}}=\frac{\text{m}}{\text{s}}
$$

So, our conversion formula is

$$
\frac{\text{cm}}{\text{s}}\cdot \frac{\text{m}}{\text{cm}}=\frac{\text{m}}{\text{s}}.
$$

Now that we have our conversion formula, we need to determine the correct numbers to use, and apply it.

- The speed given in the problem statement is $972\,\frac{\text{cm}}{\text{s}}.$

- There are $100$ centimeters per meter. Taking the reciprocal, there are $\frac{1}{100}$ meters per centimeter.

Applying our conversion formula, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}972\,\frac{\text{cm}}{\text{s}} & =972\,\frac{\text{cm}}{\text{s}}\cdot \frac{1}{100}\,\frac{\text{m}}{\text{cm}} \\  & =972\cdot \frac{1}{100}(\frac{\cancel{\text{cm}}}{\text{s}}\cdot \frac{\text{m}}{\cancel{\text{cm}}}) \\  & =9.72\,\frac{\text{m}}{\text{s}}.\end{aligned}
$$

Thus, the speed of the cruise is $9.72\,\text{m}/\text{s}.$

Question 2
?

A cruise ship on the high seas travels at a speed of 972 centimeters per second. What is the speed of the ship in meters per second?

a
97200m/s
b
0.972m/s
c
9720m/s
d
97.2m/s
e
9.72m/s
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

We are given the units cms, and we want to convert this into ms. To figure out what we need to multiply by, we can set up an equation to help us: cms⋅??=ms

We want to replace cm with m. To get rid of cm, we can put cm in the denominator so that it cancels out. To introduce m, we can put m in the numerator. cms⋅mcm=ms

So, our conversion formula is cms⋅mcm=ms.

Now that we have our conversion formula, we need to determine the correct numbers to use, and apply it.

  • The speed given in the problem statement is 972cms.
  • There are 100 centimeters per meter. Taking the reciprocal, there are 1100 meters per centimeter.

Applying our conversion formula, we have 972cms=972cms⋅1100mcm=972⋅1100(cms⋅mcm)=9.72ms.

Thus, the speed of the cruise is 9.72m/s.

q-46697.name: Question 3
q-46697.problem: A car travels at a speed of $2.5$ kilometers per minute. What is this in kilometers per hour?
q-46697.worked_solution:
We are given the units $\frac{\text{km}}{\text{min}},$ and we want to convert this into $\frac{\text{km}}{\text{hour}}.$ To figure out what we need to multiply by, we can set up an equation to help us:

$$
\frac{\text{km}}{\text{min}}\cdot \,\frac{?}{?}=\frac{\text{km}}{\text{hour}}
$$

We want to replace $\text{min}$ with $\text{hour}.$ To get rid of $\text{min},$ we can put $\text{min}$ in the numerator so that it cancels out. To introduce $\text{hour},$ we can put $\text{hour}$ in the denominator.

$$
\frac{\text{km}}{\cancel{\text{min}}}\cdot \frac{\cancel{\text{min}}}{\text{hour}}=\frac{\text{km}}{\text{hour}}
$$

So, our conversion formula is

$$
\frac{\text{km}}{\text{min}}\cdot \frac{\text{min}}{\text{hour}}=\frac{\text{km}}{\text{hour}}.
$$

Now that we have our conversion formula, we need to determine the correct numbers to use, and apply it.

- The rate given in the problem statement is $2.5\,\frac{\text{km}}{\text{min}}.$

- There are $60$ minutes in one hour.

Applying our conversion formula, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}2.5\,\frac{\text{km}}{\text{min}} & =2.5\,\frac{\text{km}}{\text{min}}\cdot 60\,\frac{\text{min}}{\text{hour}} \\  & =2.5\cdot 60(\frac{\text{km}}{\cancel{\text{min}}}\cdot \frac{\cancel{\text{min}}}{\text{hour}}) \\  & =150\,\frac{\text{km}}{\text{hour}}.\end{aligned}
$$

q-46697.html:
Question 3
?

A car travels at a speed of 2.5 kilometers per minute. What is this in kilometers per hour?

a
1500
b
600
c
15
d
150
e
60
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

We are given the units kmmin, and we want to convert this into kmhour. To figure out what we need to multiply by, we can set up an equation to help us: kmmin⋅??=kmhour

We want to replace min with hour. To get rid of min, we can put min in the numerator so that it cancels out. To introduce hour, we can put hour in the denominator. kmmin⋅minhour=kmhour

So, our conversion formula is kmmin⋅minhour=kmhour.

Now that we have our conversion formula, we need to determine the correct numbers to use, and apply it.

  • The rate given in the problem statement is 2.5kmmin.
  • There are 60 minutes in one hour.

Applying our conversion formula, we have 2.5kmmin=2.5kmmin⋅60minhour=2.5⋅60(kmmin⋅minhour)=150kmhour.
q-46697.knowledge_point: Performing a Unit Conversion: Converting a Denominator

q-105556.name: Question 4
q-105556.problem: A racecar can reach a speed of $360$ kilometers per hour. What is this speed in kilometers per second?
q-105556.worked_solution:
We are given the units $\frac{\text{km}}{\text{h}},$ and we want to convert this into $\frac{\text{km}}{\text{s}}.$ To figure out what we need to multiply by, we can set up an equation to help us:

$$
\frac{\text{km}}{\text{h}}\cdot \,\frac{?}{?}=\frac{\text{km}}{\text{s}}
$$

We want to replace $\text{h}$ with $\text{s}.$ To get rid of $\text{h},$ we can put $\text{h}$ in the numerator so that it cancels out. To introduce $\text{s},$ we can put $\text{s}$ in the denominator.

$$
\frac{\text{km}}{\cancel{\text{h}}}\cdot \frac{\cancel{\text{h}}}{\text{s}}=\frac{\text{km}}{\text{s}}
$$

So, our conversion formula is

$$
\frac{\text{km}}{\text{h}}\cdot \frac{\text{h}}{\text{s}}=\frac{\text{km}}{\text{s}}.
$$

Now that we have our conversion formula, we need to determine the correct numbers to use, and apply it.

- The speed given in the problem statement is $360\,\frac{\text{km}}{\text{h}}.$

- There are $3\,600$ seconds per hour. Taking the reciprocal, there are $\frac{1}{3\,600}$ hours per second.

Applying our conversion formula, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}360\,\frac{\text{km}}{\text{h}} & =360\,\frac{\text{km}}{\text{h}}\cdot \frac{1}{3\,600}\,\frac{\text{h}}{\text{s}} \\  & =(360\cdot \frac{1}{3\,600})\,\frac{\text{km}}{\cancel{\text{h}}}\cdot \frac{\cancel{\text{h}}}{\text{s}} \\  & =0.1\,\frac{\text{km}}{\text{s}}.\end{aligned}
$$

Thus, the race car reach a speed  of $0.1\,\text{km}/\text{s}.$

q-105556.html:
Question 4
?

A racecar can reach a speed of 360 kilometers per hour. What is this speed in kilometers per second?

a
0.01kms
b
0.6kms
c
6kms
d
10kms
e
0.1kms
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

We are given the units kmh, and we want to convert this into kms. To figure out what we need to multiply by, we can set up an equation to help us: kmh⋅??=kms

We want to replace h with s. To get rid of h, we can put h in the numerator so that it cancels out. To introduce s, we can put s in the denominator. kmh⋅hs=kms

So, our conversion formula is kmh⋅hs=kms.

Now that we have our conversion formula, we need to determine the correct numbers to use, and apply it.

  • The speed given in the problem statement is 360kmh.
  • There are 3600 seconds per hour. Taking the reciprocal, there are 13600 hours per second.

Applying our conversion formula, we have 360kmh=360kmh⋅13600hs=(360⋅13600)kmh⋅hs=0.1kms.

Thus, the race car reach a speed of 0.1km/s.

q-52044.name: Question 5
q-52044.problem: A tree sapling grows by $2$ centimeters per day. Assuming that one year has $365$ days, how many meters does the tree grow in one year?
q-52044.worked_solution:
We are given the units $\frac{\text{cm}}{\text{day}},$ and we want to convert this into $\frac{\text{m}}{\text{year}}.$ We're converting two units instead of just one, so we're going to have to multiply by two conversion factors:

$$
\frac{\text{cm}}{\text{day}}\cdot \,\frac{?}{?}\cdot \,\frac{?}{?}=\frac{\text{m}}{\text{year}}
$$

One of the conversion factors should change $\text{cm}$ to $\text{m}.$

$$
\frac{\cancel{\text{cm}}}{\text{day}}\cdot \frac{\text{m}}{\cancel{\text{cm}}}\cdot \,\frac{?}{?}=\frac{\text{m}}{\text{year}}
$$

The other conversion factor should change $\text{day}$ into $\text{year}.$

$$
\frac{\cancel{\text{cm}}}{\cancel{\text{day}}}\cdot \frac{\text{m}}{\cancel{\text{cm}}}\cdot \frac{\cancel{\text{days}}}{\text{year}}=\frac{\text{m}}{\text{year}}
$$

So, our conversion formula is

$$
\frac{\text{cm}}{\text{day}}\cdot \frac{\text{m}}{\text{cm}}\cdot \frac{\text{days}}{\text{year}}=\frac{\text{m}}{\text{year}}.
$$

Now that we have our conversion formula, we need to determine the correct numbers to use, and apply it.

- The rate given in the problem statement is $2\,\frac{\text{cm}}{\text{day}}.$

- There are $100$ centimeters in one meter, therefore, there are $\frac{1}{100}$ meters in one centimeter.

- There are $365$ days in one year.

Applying our conversion formula, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}2\,\frac{\text{cm}}{\text{day}} & =2\,\frac{\text{cm}}{\text{day}}\cdot \frac{1}{100}\,\frac{\text{m}}{\text{cm}}\cdot 365\,\frac{\text{days}}{\text{year}} \\  & =2\cdot \frac{1}{100}\cdot 365(\frac{\cancel{\text{cm}}}{\cancel{\text{day}}}\cdot \frac{\text{m}}{\cancel{\text{cm}}}\cdot \frac{\cancel{\text{days}}}{\text{year}}) \\  & =7.3\,\frac{\text{m}}{\text{year}}.\end{aligned}
$$

Consequently, $2$ centimeters per day is equivalent to $7.3$ meters per year. In one year, the tree grows by $7.3$ meters.

q-52044.html:
Question 5
?

A tree sapling grows by 2 centimeters per day. Assuming that one year has 365 days, how many meters does the tree grow in one year?

a
8.1 meters
b
6.5 meters
c
7.3 meters
d
6.9 meters
e
7.8 meters
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

We are given the units cmday, and we want to convert this into myear. We're converting two units instead of just one, so we're going to have to multiply by two conversion factors: cmday⋅??⋅??=myear

One of the conversion factors should change cm to m. cmday⋅mcm⋅??=myear

The other conversion factor should change day into year. cmday⋅mcm⋅daysyear=myear

So, our conversion formula is cmday⋅mcm⋅daysyear=myear.

Now that we have our conversion formula, we need to determine the correct numbers to use, and apply it.

  • The rate given in the problem statement is 2cmday.
  • There are 100 centimeters in one meter, therefore, there are 1100 meters in one centimeter.
  • There are 365 days in one year.

Applying our conversion formula, we have 2cmday=2cmday⋅1100mcm⋅365daysyear=2⋅1100⋅365(cmday⋅mcm⋅daysyear)=7.3myear.

Consequently, 2 centimeters per day is equivalent to 7.3 meters per year. In one year, the tree grows by 7.3 meters.

q-52042.name: Question 6
q-52042.problem: Lewis spends $0.5$ hours per day studying. How many minutes per week does Lewis study for?
q-52042.worked_solution:
We are given the units $\frac{\text{hours}}{\text{day}},$ and we want to convert this into $\frac{\text{min}}{\text{week}}.$ We're converting two units instead of just one, so we're going to have to multiply by two conversion factors:

$$
\frac{\text{hours}}{\text{day}}\cdot \,\frac{?}{?}\cdot \,\frac{?}{?}=\frac{\text{min}}{\text{week}}
$$

One of the conversion factors should change $\text{hours}$ to $\text{min}.$

$$
\frac{\cancel{\text{hours}}}{\text{day}}\cdot \frac{\text{min}}{\cancel{\text{hour}}}\cdot \,\frac{?}{?}=\frac{\text{m}}{\text{s}}
$$

The other conversion factor should change $\text{day}$ into $\text{week}.$

$$
\frac{\cancel{\text{hours}}}{\cancel{\text{day}}}\cdot \frac{\text{min}}{\cancel{\text{hour}}}\cdot \frac{\cancel{\text{days}}}{\text{week}}=\frac{\text{min}}{\text{week}}
$$

So, our conversion formula is

$$
\frac{\text{hours}}{\text{day}}\cdot \frac{\text{min}}{\text{hour}}\cdot \frac{\text{days}}{\text{week}}=\frac{\text{min}}{\text{week}}.
$$

Now that we have our conversion formula, we need to determine the correct numbers to use, and apply it.

- The rate given in the problem statement is $0.5\,\frac{\text{hours}}{\text{day}}.$

- There are $60$ minutes per hour.

- There are $7$ days per week.

Applying our conversion formula, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}0.5\,\frac{\text{hours}}{\text{day}} & =0.5\,\frac{\text{hours}}{\text{day}}\cdot 60\,\frac{\text{min}}{\text{hour}}\cdot 7\,\frac{\text{days}}{\text{week}} \\  & =(0.5\cdot 60\cdot 7)\,\frac{\cancel{\text{hours}}}{\cancel{\text{day}}}\cdot \frac{\text{min}}{\cancel{\text{hour}}}\cdot \frac{\cancel{\text{days}}}{\text{week}} \\  & =210\,\frac{\text{min}}{\text{week}}.\end{aligned}
$$

Thus, Lewis studies at a rate of $210\,\text{min/week}.$

q-52042.html:
Question 6
?

Lewis spends 0.5 hours per day studying. How many minutes per week does Lewis study for?

a
150min/week
b
175min/week
c
210min/week
d
250min/week
e
160min/week
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

We are given the units hoursday, and we want to convert this into minweek. We're converting two units instead of just one, so we're going to have to multiply by two conversion factors:

hoursday⋅??⋅??=minweek

One of the conversion factors should change hours to min.

hoursday⋅minhour⋅??=ms

The other conversion factor should change day into week.

hoursday⋅minhour⋅daysweek=minweek

So, our conversion formula is

hoursday⋅minhour⋅daysweek=minweek.

Now that we have our conversion formula, we need to determine the correct numbers to use, and apply it.

  • The rate given in the problem statement is 0.5hoursday.
  • There are 60 minutes per hour.
  • There are 7 days per week.

Applying our conversion formula, we have 0.5hoursday=0.5hoursday⋅60minhour⋅7daysweek=(0.5⋅60⋅7)hoursday⋅minhour⋅daysweek=210minweek.

Thus, Lewis studies at a rate of 210min/week.
